newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares dip, volume low despite longer day.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares dip, volume low despite longer day.

text.p: Swedish shares edged down on the first day of extended trading on Monday, and brokers blamed the Labor Day holiday in the U.S. and the end of the first half reporting season for the listless, low-volume trade.

The all-share index closed 0.01 percent lower at 1980.66 in volume of 2.2 billion crowns. The best performing sector of the day was banking and insurance, which climbed 0.58 percent despite rising debt yields.
Monday was the debut for extended trading in Stockholm, where bourse hours are now 0800 GMT to 1500 GMT. Dealers said the Stock Exchange could have picked a better debut day.
"There's been a lack of volumes with the U.S. closed. There will of course be more trade in time, but some transactions will simply be postponed," one broker said.
Ericsson lost 2.0 crowns to 152.5 and Volvo dipped 0.5 crowns to 140.5, but Astra held steady at 280 crowns.
Banking and financial shares were the day's main winners, with Skandia gaining 3.0 crowns to 158.5 and Handelsbanken picked up 0.5 crowns to 136.
Dealers said the undertone of the bourse was strong, surpringly so in view of the fall in U.S. share prices over the past few weeks.
"I'm surprised it's so stable, I could have bet money it would have gone down. But then most of the trade is in second liners with the Americans out of the market," one broker said.
